newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar firm but off highs after nearing 124 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firm but off highs after nearing 124 yen.

text.p: *Dollar steady to slightly firmer in early Tokyo, but off earlier highs after edging within reach of fresh four-year high of 124 yen touched overnight in Europe.
*Profit taking emerged as operators lightened positions ahead of U.S. jobs data, due out later today, and G7 meeting on Saturday. Some exporter selling also likely.
*Dollar moved as high as 123.97 yen in early Asian trade.
*Although support expected to hold solid from 123.30-50 yen, where importer bids are placed, little active buying detected in early Tokyo.

*"There's no real need to rush to either buy or sell ahead of the jobs data and G7, although some operators are taking the chance to lighten their positions a bit just in case," one trust bank dealer said.

*Dollar expected to remain supported as market sense that little will be done at G7 besides calling for more stable exchange rates has been strengthened by statements from various monetary authorities.
*On Thursday, German Finance Ministry characterised recent moves in currency markets as a "normalisation" from conditions prevailing in early 1995.
*German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt and French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis also endorsed recent currency moves.
*Market will closely watch moves in cross-trading, as energy, if any, likely to emerge from there today.
*Sterling weaker after facing heavy profit-taking overnight, but still holding above 202 yen. Mark at high end of 74-yen level.
*Dollar to remain strong against mark after sharply higher German unemployment figures were released Thursday, showing jobless rate increasing to 12.2 percent in January.
*German unemployment surged by more than half million to post-war record of 4.66 million in January.
*Japan Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told news conference that Japan will go to G7 with stance that overly weak or strong yen unfavourable.
*He added that he believed G7 nations agree that stable foreign exchange markets are important for each economy.
*Mitsuzuka said he will meet German Finance Minister Theo Waigel at conference, and is in process of scheduling meeting with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
